headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: Authelia’s broad network/OIDC role can feed a write-capable marketing skill chain with unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia has no shared channel or file bridge documented, while marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skills files and can read/write local files. That makes prompt injection plausible only if an operator manually routes Authelia output into those files or prompts. The pathway is not default, so low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF an operator copies Authelia output into marketingskills skill files or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Authelia and marketingskills in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of model output into skill files.
Add a human review step before any skill-file edits.
Use read-only mounts for Authelia outputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared context files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia touches no data classes in the profile, while marketingskills touches marketing content and can read/write files. There is no documented shared workspace, same OAuth principal, or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is limited to unusual operator-created sharing. Uncertainty is low because the pairwise data path is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, marketingskills can read Authelia-generated artifacts.
IF Authelia is configured to handle secrets or identity data outside this profile, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place Authelia outputs in shared folders.
Separate credentials and API tokens per agent.
Review file permissions on any shared workspace.
Delete transient artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth API calls, while marketingskills can read and write files, spawn subprocesses, and use allowlisted network egress. Their write surfaces overlap only indirectly, but both can mutate shared resources if co-located. Because the profiles do not prove locking or isolation, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF both agents share an OAuth-backed resource, conflicting updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo.
Check for stale files before each write.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication/authorization decisions, and marketingskills is designed to build on shared context and files. If Authelia output is treated as authoritative by marketingskills, errors can cascade into downstream marketing artifacts or actions. The pair lacks verification controls in the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes Authelia output without verification, incorrect auth context can propagate.
IF Authelia-derived text is inserted into shared context files, downstream outputs may inherit errors.
mitigations: Require human verification of Authelia-derived inputs.
Mark Authelia outputs as untrusted in prompts.
Keep source and derived files separate.
Add a checklist for downstream factual claims.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation before reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with broad network egress, while marketingskills handles marketing content and local files. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and Authelia’s profile shows no touched data classes. Compliance risk is therefore limited to operator-chosen data placement rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in marketingskills files, compliance review is required.
IF Authelia is configured to process identity data outside this profile, residency or retention issues may arise.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in marketing skill files.
Review retention settings for shared artifacts.
Keep identity data out of marketing workflows.
Document data flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data paths.
